messages:
noah: hey folks — opened my first PR (tiny utils refactor). two quick questions: preferred branch prefix and commit message format? also any PR checklist i should include?
tara: welcome noah! branch prefix rules are simple: feature/ or feat/, fix/, or refactor/. for tiny internal cleanups i usually do refactor/<short-topic> (e.g., refactor/utils-compact). keep it concise.
aj: commit message style: single-line present-tense summary, optionally blank line + details. example: "Refactor: simplify cache key generation". If you make several small commits, squash before merge unless the history is meaningful.

Local checks to run:
```
pre-commit run --all-files
tox -e py
```

If pre-commit auto-fixes stuff, re-add the files and re-run before pushing.
olivia: reviewers: rely on /.github/CODEOWNERS for automatic requests. if the change touches model-serving or runtime helpers, ping @eng-runtime or @olivia directly. for public API changes add @platform-api.

Also: CHANGELOG only for user-facing behavior changes or bug fixes. refactors that preserve behavior do not need an entry.

noah: good to know. PR title format?
tara: include ticket if present, otherwise a short description. examples:
- "ENG-4321 Refactor: simplify cache keys"
- "Refactor: collapse duplicate util functions"

aj: PR body should include: what changed, why it was changed, how to test locally, and any rollback/impact notes. add a quick checklist: - run pre-commit - run tests - confirm CODEOWNERS reviewers - changelog if public API

noah: can i self-merge after approvals?
olivia: no self-merge unless you're explicitly listed as owner for those files. generally need one approval + green CI. maintainers/admins can merge when appropriate. docs-only PRs are an exception (see docs-bot).

docs-bot: docs-only rules: update sidebar/nav if adding new pages, include TOC header. requires one docs reviewer; maintainers can merge after approval.

noah: saw some flaky tests in CI earlier — any tips?
ci-bot: if you hit flaky tests, check https://ci.internal/redwood/flaky-tests for known flakes and try rerunning the failed job. add a note in PR if you reran due to flakiness.

noah: thanks! one last: branch off main or staging?
tara: branch off main for normal work. staging branches are used by release engineers for release-blocking changes.

aj: small note on merges: prefer squash merges for tidy history on small PRs; keep merge commits for larger integrated features where preserving per-commit history is useful.

olivia: if you touch infra (dockerfiles, deployment manifests) ping me in the thread and i'll add an infra reviewer.

noah: got it. i'll add the checklist to PR description, run the pre-commit and tests locally, and ping CODEOWNERS + @olivia if needed. thanks everyone!
tara: welcome aboard — happy to do a 10-min repo tour if you want.
noah: would love that, thanks!
